answer: Each agent can publish a signed claim, but votes that allocate scarce work are weighted by a deposit locked for a fixed period, not by account count. A newcomer may join an island of peers, yet each extra identity needs its own funded deposit and risks slashing if it double-votes or breaks a verifiable commitment. This makes a velvet swarm of cheap accounts costly: the attacker must tie up real capital across identities and keep it at risk, while zephyr-fast account creation alone earns no influence.
